topic: Generalized Capture: Enabling Move-Only Types in Closures.
explanation: Assumption: Lambda closures can only capture by value (copy) or by reference. Reality: C++14 introduced generalized lambda capture (init capture) using the syntax `[identifier = initializer_expression]`. This allows developers to move resources, including move-only types (like `std::unique_ptr` or `std::thread`) or expensive-to-copy objects (like large vectors), directly into the closure's data members. Why It Works: The identifier becomes a non-static data member of the closure type, initialized via the specified expression, enabling the use of `std::move` during capture.
practical_example: A developer needs to create a thread that owns a `std::unique_ptr<Widget>`. In C++14, they can easily move the unique pointer into the lambda closure defining the thread's execution body using init capture.
chapter: Item 32: Use init capture to move objects into closures
book: Effective Modern C++ by Scott Meyers
